d: Computing where the arm's hand is, and which way it points, from the joint angles.
The set of all points the arm's hand can reach.
A quantity with a length and a direction, drawn as an arrow. Where the arrow starts doesn't matter.
How far a vector goes along one axis, for example its x component. It can be negative.
How long a vector is: the square root of the sum of its squared components. Never negative.
A vector of length one. It gives a direction without a distance; frame axes are unit vectors.
An origin plus one unit vector per axis, at right angles to each other. Positions are measured from it; frames are named like {A}.
The point a frame measures from: where its axes start.
The vector from a frame's origin to a point. Its components are the point's coordinates in that frame.
A 3D frame where the right hand's fingers curl from x to y and the thumb points along z. The course uses only these.
